## FAQ **Q1. 半導體專案工程師跟一般營造業的工地主任有什麼不同？**: ## FAQ **Q1. How is a semiconductor project engineer different from a site manager in general construction?** A1. The main difference is what you are building. A semiconductor project engineer supervises construction and inspects quality at high-tech fabs (cleanrooms, process piping, MEP systems), and on top of what a normal building site involves, has to coordinate process-related interfaces. For example, a fab's MEP systems must be built to match the specifications of semiconductor equipment, so the requirements for precision and cleanliness are higher than on ordinary construction projects. **Q2. Do I need a civil engineering or architecture degree to apply?** A2. Not necessarily. The education requirement covers five fields: electrical engineering, mechanical engineering (including HVAC/refrigeration and energy programs), industrial design, civil engineering (including construction), and architecture. Any junior college or higher degree in one of these counts; it is not limited to civil engineering or architecture backgrounds. **Q3. Is the work different between the trainee and senior positions?** A3. The core duties are the same (on-site schedule control, quality inspection, subcontractor coordination, MEP supervision). The differences are the starting pay and the experience required: the senior position pays NT$50,000–60,000 a month and requires prior experience supervising semiconductor fab or fab-office construction and MEP work; the trainee position pays NT$35,000–45,000 a month, requires no related experience, but does require a strong willingness to learn. **Q4. Will I be reassigned often? Will I have to move a lot?** A4. Assignments follow current project locations in Taoyuan/Hsinchu/Miaoli, Taichung, and Yunlin. Staff from other counties are provided with dormitories, usually not far from the site, plus a monthly home-visit travel allowance and a fuel allowance for project assignments to reduce the actual burden of working away from home. The exact frequency and location of assignments depend on the projects underway at the time, so we recommend asking the hiring department directly about current project locations when you apply. **Q5. Am I at a disadvantage without the relevant certificates?** A5. Certificates such as Public Works Quality Management Personnel and Class A Occupational Safety and Health Supervisor for the construction industry, as well as AutoCAD drafting or drawing-reading skills, are pluses, not requirements. Having them will improve your salary offer, but you can still apply without them; the trainee track in particular is designed for people without related experience or certificates. **Q6. Is the salary fixed with no raises?** A6. No. Your starting salary is set based on your past experience, professional skills, and interview performance, and after you join, raises are based on performance. It is not a fixed pay structure. ## Sources - 104 (a Taiwanese job site), "2026 Semiconductor Talent Report," as reported by the Commercial Times (Taiwan) in "Semiconductor Expansion Sparks Scramble for Construction Workers; Average Annual Pay for This Role Tops NT$1.72 Million," 2026-09-13: https://www.ctee.com.tw/news/20260913700008-431003 (verified 2026-09-23; report published 2026-09-08) - Job requirements, pay, benefits, and duties: data from the semiconductor project engineer position Step1ne is currently recruiting for, verified 2026-09-23
## FAQ **Q1. 工程設計工程師完全不用進工地嗎？** A1. 不是。工: ## FAQ **Q1. Do engineering design engineers never have to go on site?** A1. No. The work environment for engineering design engineers is also listed as "100% on site." They are stationed at the project's site office and help with site surveys and with checking that drawings match actual construction. Their main output is still drawings, not site management. **Q2. Do site (project) engineers have to know AutoCAD?** A2. Not necessarily. In the job requirements, AutoCAD drafting or drawing-reading skills are a plus, not a requirement. The real requirements are communication and coordination skills, willingness to be assigned to project locations, and basic office skills. Knowing the software can earn you a better salary offer, but it is not a condition for applying. **Q3. Which path pays more?** A3. The salary ranges overlap, so neither is simply higher. The trainee track on both sides pays NT$35,000–45,000 per month, and the experienced track on both sides pays NT$50,000–60,000 per month. Actual pay depends on your background, skills and interview performance. The difference lies in the job content, not the starting pay structure. **Q4. Can I apply to either path without a related degree?** A4. Neither trainee track requires related work experience, but there are still degree requirements. The design side focuses on industrial design, civil engineering (including construction) and architecture (or interior design). The site side is broader and also includes electrical engineering and mechanical engineering (including refrigeration/HVAC and energy). As long as your major is within range, you can apply for the trainee positions without hands-on experience. **Q5. Can I switch between the design side and the site side later?** A5. The positions themselves don't restrict switching, but in practice the two sides build different skills. The design side builds drafting and drawing-integration skills, while the site side builds hands-on site management and coordination. Changing direction usually means filling in the core skills the other path requires (for example, moving from design to site means gaining site management experience; moving from site to design means building advanced drafting skills). **Q6. Is "construction supervision" (監造) the same as the site (project) engineer described here?** A6. Not exactly. Under Taiwanese regulations, "construction supervision" is an independent third-party role appointed by the project owner to check that the contractor builds according to the drawings. The site (project) engineer discussed here is an internal job title at a private engineering company, focused on site schedule control, quality inspection and subcontractor coordination. The duties are similar, but the legal status is different. If this distinction matters to you, we suggest confirming the role directly with the hiring team when you apply. ## Sources - Job content, salary, education and certification requirements for engineering design engineers / site (semiconductor project) engineers: data from Step1ne's open positions "Senior Engineering Design Engineer," "Trainee Engineering Design Engineer," "Senior Semiconductor Project Engineer" and "Trainee Semiconductor Project Engineer," Step1ne D1 database, verified 2026-09-30 - General explanation of the career split between design and site roles: "A Complete Overview of 6 Types of Engineers: The Engineering Job Map Employers and Job Seekers Need to Know," HNL Consultants: https://www.hnl-consultants.com/%E5%B7%A5%E7%A8%8B%E5%B8%AB/ (verified 2026-09-30) - Legal definition and scope of construction supervision: "Construction Supervision Explained: Quality Control, Schedule and Safety Duties," TWProbe房產觀測站: https://twprobe.com/jianzhu-gongcheng-jianzao-zhineng-zongjian-zhinan/ (verified 2026-09-30)

<p>BIM 工程師(儲備培訓)</p><h3>工作內容</h3><h4>BIM:
BIM Engineer (Trainee Program)

Responsibilities

BIM modeling and coordination

  • Build and revise BIM models in AutoCAD and Revit
  • BIM coordination and drawing reviews

On-site collaboration

  • Assist with site surveys at the construction site
  • Handle tasks assigned by your supervisor

On-the-job training

  • Carry out BIM work under the project contract while receiving the company's full training

Requirements

Must have
  • Willing to work full-time on site and follow the site schedule (two days off a week, no rotating shifts)
  • Able to work fully on site at the Houli, Taichung plant area long term
  • After being hired, complete 6 hours of occupational safety training and obtain the certificate before your start date (the construction-industry "green card"; you can take the course near you and claim the cost back from the company with a receipt)
Nice to have
  • Experience with AutoCAD, Revit or other drafting/modeling software is a plus
  • Engineering or design-related work experience is a plus
  • Interest in BIM or construction, and keen to learn and grow within an on-site team

BIM Engineer (Trainee)

<p>供應鏈管理及國際貿易業務主管</p><h3>工作內容</h3><h4>供應:
Head of Supply Chain Management and International Trade Sales

Responsibilities

Supply chain strategy and integration

  • Set the group's supply chain strategy, connecting demand forecasting, procurement, production coordination, inventory and logistics
  • Integrate supply and delivery across plants in Cambodia and the Philippines and OEM partner factories in the US
  • Improve delivery efficiency and optimize overall cost while balancing revenue, gross margin, cost and inventory targets

Procurement and supplier management

  • Lead supplier development, evaluation and contract negotiations
  • Define procurement strategy to ensure the quality, lead times and stable supply of raw materials and products
  • Build supplier performance management and risk backup mechanisms

Overseas markets and key accounts

  • Expand overseas markets, key accounts and channels, and set the overseas market development strategy
  • Lead pricing and commercial negotiations, with accountability for revenue and gross margin targets
  • Analyze market trends, identify new business opportunities and maintain relationships with international customers

Cross-border orders and risk control

  • Oversee import/export, cross-border order fulfillment and cross-border logistics
  • Work with finance, legal and other teams to manage trade compliance, customer credit and collection risk

Team leadership and operations analysis

  • Lead domestic and overseas teams (about 10 people at the start, covering supply chain and export sales), driving cross-functional collaboration, performance management and process improvement
  • Track cost, lead times and inventory with operating data, and regularly present operations analysis and strategic recommendations to the CEO / President

Group strategic projects and digital transformation

  • Execute cross-border and strategic projects assigned by the General Manager
  • Take part in digitalizing the group's supply chain: automating load planning, freight rate comparison and shipment tracking, plus a supply chain data dashboard (a direction disclosed in the annual report)
  • The group uses Digiwin ERP and continues to push AI and digital adoption

Requirements

Required
  • Bachelor's degree or above
  • 15+ years in the textile and apparel industry, including at least 5 years in a manager-level or higher role
  • A track record in supply chain integration and international trade / overseas sales management, able to balance revenue, gross margin, cost and inventory at the same time
  • Well versed in international business negotiation, import/export and cross-border logistics
  • Experience leading multinational teams, with strong cross-functional integration skills
  • Fluent in Chinese and English; able to chair meetings, negotiate and review business documents in English independently (TOEIC 750 or above)
  • Familiar with AI tools and applications and Office software; able to work independently
Preferred
  • Experience in medical devices, medical consumables, protective equipment or textile manufacturing
  • Experience managing overseas production bases or a multi-site supply chain
  • Has led a supply chain transformation or held profit-and-loss responsibility for a business unit
  • Familiar with ERP systems and supply chain digitalization; OEM/ODM or B2B sales experience
  • A second foreign language (Japanese preferred)

<strong>代招</strong>（正式名稱是「委託招募」或「正職代招」）是: Outsourced recruitment (formally "commissioned recruitment" or "permanent placement") means a company pays a consulting firm to find, screen, and schedule interviews with candidates, and once hired, the employee is still the company's own full-time employee; the employer does not change. Fees are usually success-based, charged only when the candidate starts. At Step1ne, for example, the average is from 1.5 months' salary, depending on the difficulty of the role and the contract. Under Taiwanese regulations, there is a cap on what a recruitment agency can charge an employer; it cannot charge whatever it likes. It differs from headhunting mainly in the seniority targeted and how candidates are approached, and from staffing in "who the employer is."
<strong>代招公司須有合法許可</strong>：從事私立就業服務業務須向: Recruitment agencies must be properly licensed: providing private employment services requires a license from the competent authority, and operating without one is prohibited
<strong>代招（委託招募）</strong>是企業付費請顧問公司代為找人、: Recruiting services (contingency recruitment) means a company pays a consulting firm to find, screen, and schedule interviews with candidates on its behalf; once hired, the employee is the company's own permanent staff. Most firms use a success-based fee, charged only when the candidate starts work. At Step1ne, fees start at roughly 1.5 months' salary on average (actual terms depend on the role and the contract), and Taiwan's regulations also set a fee cap. For a full explanation of fees, process, and how it differs from executive search, see What is a recruiting agency? Fees, process, and how it differs from executive search.

商業計畫書的架構其實很標準，摘要、市場、產品、營運、<strong>團隊</st: The structure of a business plan is actually quite standard: executive summary, market, product, operations, team, financials, timeline, and risks — eight sections, with plenty of templates online. What really sets plans apart is the “team and staffing” chapter, which is exactly the one most people write carelessly. Take Taiwan's government grant programs: reviewers explicitly list “the reasonableness of staffing and budget allocation” as a key criterion, and they look not only at degrees but also at the actual experience of R&D staff. You can copy the structure; you can't copy the staffing chapter.

工程設計工程師跟現場工程師，職稱聽起來很像，實際做的事一樣嗎？: Engineering design engineers and site engineers sound alike—do they actually do the same work?
Engineering design engineers and site (project) engineers are both called engineers and their pay ranges overlap (both NT$35,000–45,000 during training and NT$50,000–60,000 at senior level), but the actual work is different. Design engineers mainly produce drawings in AutoCAD and Revit—their focus is the drawings. Site (project) engineers mainly track construction progress, run quality inspections and coordinate with subcontractors—their focus is people and the site. Both go to the construction site (neither is a pure desk job); the difference is that design engineers go to check the drawings against reality, while site engineers go to manage progress. Which path to choose depends on whether you'd rather get the details exactly right on paper or work through problems with people on site.

比較少被提到的是：向雇主收取的代招費用，其實<strong>受法規上限規範</s: What gets mentioned less often is that the fees an agency charges employers are actually capped by regulation. Under Article 3 of Taiwan's Standards for Fee Items and Amounts Charged by Private Employment Service Institutions, the registration and placement fees a for-profit employment service agency charges an employer may not, in total, exceed the hire's first month of salary if that salary is at or below the average wage published by the central competent authority; if it is above the average wage, the total may not exceed four months of the hire's salary. In addition, the service fee per employee may not exceed NT$2,000 per year (Laws & Regulations Database (Taiwan), Standards for Fee Items and Amounts Charged by Private Employment Service Institutions, Article 3). In other words, as long as a quote stays within the legal cap, the fee structure and amount are agreed in the contract between both parties; before you sign, you can ask the agency to explain the basis for its quote.
